title: Sample 13-12: Lines of Poetry with Stress and Meter

illustrates.quote: Transcribe a poem that contains stress, scansion, or meter marks twice. Place the two versions on a single braille page if possible. The first version should include the title and author or other attribution.

blocks.features: Italic work-title, parenthetical extent and meter note.

First two stanzas of Blake's "The Piper" (from Songs of Innocence), each syllable's stress marked in print with a breve or acute accent above it; print excerpt is torn off after the fourth line, before further (unshown) stanza content.

lines.text: On a cloud I saw a child,
And he laughing said to me:

print.notes: Picture spanning PDF pp.380-381 (title/rule text/first writing's transcriber's note on p.380, continuing to the first and second braille writings on p.381; the poem's braille content itself is entirely on p.381, matching the source's own page break falling between the two).
print.printFeatures: Plain text author/title lines; breve/acute stress marks above individual syllables of each print line.

pageBreaks.note: The reference-line numbering restarts at 1 after braille line 19 (source ref '20', .txt line 10987, a full-blank stress-diagram spacer row -- genuine numbered content, not page filler) -- no explicit —New Braille Page— marker text in the source. uncertain: Blank-line placement around the SECOND writing's four poetic lines (each shown here with a preceding blank row before its stress-symbol diagram) was read directly off the two source pages; the exact blank-line count immediately either side of the braille page break (between 'us$3' and the continuation) was not independently re-verified beyond what the .txt shows.
resolution: Every leading-space count independently re-derived character-by-character against the source (.txt lines 10968-10987 page 1, 10994-11010 page 2; both pages' reference-number field is 5 characters -- 2-digit max (17/19) + 3). Two lines needed a NEW value neither run had (index 0, 'William Blake' byline: 12 leading blank cells, centring a 16-character line in 40 cells -- both runs had 11; index 1, 'The Piper' title: 14 leading blank cells, centring a 12-character line in 40 cells -- run A had 10, run B had 13) and two more needed a value NEITHER run had (index 25: 5, both runs undercounted -- run A 3, run B 4; index 26: 4, run A 2, run B 3). Index 2 (caption line) matches run A's count (5); indices 33/34 match run B's counts (5/4, run A overcounted at 6/2). The page break was represented as a literal form-feed character prefixed to run B's resuming line (index 20) -- removed here since no gold file anywhere in this repository embeds a form-feed inside braille.lines; the established convention (section-9/11/16 precedent) is a separate braille.pageBreaks entry instead, added above. All other lines (29 of 37) were already identical between the two runs and independently confirmed correct against the source.
